newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile NAFTA deal must include labour rules - unions.
newsitem.headline: Chile NAFTA deal must include labour rules - unions.

text.p: Chile's largest trade union body demanded on Friday the inclusion of labour and environment clauses in any deal to extend the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA) to Chile.
Employment rules are necessary to stop Chile from becoming "a marketplace for cheap labour and inhuman working conditions," said a statement by the Central Unitaria de Trabajadores (CUT).
Chile's long-delayed bid to join NAFTA was revived this week during President Eduardo Frei's visit to the United States during which he held talks with President Bill Clinton and addressed Congress.

Clinton called on Congress to pass "fast track" legislation to allow the administration to negotiate trade accords with Chile and other Latin American countries. Talks on Chile's membership of NAFTA started in December 1994, but have gone nowhere because of the lack of "fast track" authority.
Union leaders accused Chilean companies of opposing the employment and environment clauses so that they can operate with poor labour conditions and without protecting the environment.
"Some Chilean businessmen want to compete with North American firms at the cost of bad working conditions, cheap labour and a disregard for the environnment," said CUT general secretary Maria Rozas.
Despite these concerns, trades unionists did not oppose Chile's membership in NAFTA, which links the United States, Mexico and Canada, she said.
"We support trade agreements, but not those which mean more labour exploitation," said Rozas.
Chilean ecologists opposed on Wednesday the extension of NAFTA to Chile, saying it would reduce the existing levels of environment protection.
